issues.editorNote: Issue #5 covers Sunday, June 8 through Saturday, June 14, 1986. The desk leads with the June 10 PC Magazine workstation package because it lands inside the issue week; the remaining columns draw from dated June computer magazines, same-month product notices, Billboard's June 14 Album Rock Tracks chart, and the June 13 domestic movie charts.
issues.morningLine: This week: DOS steps toward the workstation floor, expanded memory and menus crowd the PC conversation, June software shelves fill with integrated packages and games, and Ferris Bueller turns a school-day absence into a box-office fact.

lead.headline: DOS Meets the Workstation in a Busy June PC Week
lead.summary: PC Magazine's June 10 issue put the Xerox 6085 and the wider workstation question in front of IBM PC readers: high-resolution 19-inch screens, megabytes of RAM, multitasking, networking habits, and the promise of running DOS beside a stronger native environment. For an office buyer in this week, the story is not just raw speed; it is whether the familiar DOS desk can borrow workstation polish without abandoning the software shelf that made the PC useful.
lead.confidence: Exact dated June 10, 1986 magazine issue inside target week; workstation-market framing from the issue's contents and article deck

issues.editorNote: June 7, 1986 was a Saturday, so today's issue treats exact-day culture and chart material as the date anchor, while the computer desk leans on same-week trade coverage and current-shelf games.
issues.morningLine: Saturday Edition: the computer desk is quiet, the game shelf is loud, rock radio has the date stamp, and the market box carries Friday's close because Wall Street is shut.

lead.headline: Saturday Desk: The PC Standard Keeps Spreading While VisiCalc Leaves the Counter
lead.summary: For June 7 itself, the computer trade desk is quiet; the strongest personal-computer story remains the same-week VisiCalc handoff after Lotus discontinued the pioneering spreadsheet. Saturday's issue frames it as the office-software background hum behind the weekend game and BBS chatter.

computerItems.summary: InfoWorld's June 9 issue covered Epson's Equity II as a low-priced IBM-compatible challenger, a sign that clone competition was pushing business buyers toward cheaper PC-standard machines.

computerItems.label: Software

computerItems.summary: Aldus PageMaker, released for Macintosh in 1985, was still drawing serious trade-press attention in June 1986 as page layout became one of the Mac's clearest professional strengths.

computerItems.summary: Nintendo released the Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2 for the Famicom Disk System on June 3, while Enix's Dragon Quest, released May 27, was still new on Famicom shelves.
